name: Khmer Empire

areaKm2.note: Seshat codes 939,245 km2 for Classical Angkor (1100, mid); the Khmer Empire infobox gives 1,000,000 km2 for 1290 (Turchin et al., high). The world_1200 Khmer Empire polygon measures 0.52 million km2 on the sphere (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aourednik/historical-basemaps/master/geojson/world_1200.geojson, low) and omits occupied Champa.

population.note: Educated guess. Seshat codes 1,500,000 for Classical Angkor in 1100 (https://seshat-db.com/core/polity/41, low) but says the empire total is unclear; Greater Angkor alone held 700,000-900,000 in the 13th century (Klassen et al., Khmer Empire page). HYDE 1200: Cambodia 1.2M, Thailand 1.4M, Laos 0.3M, Vietnam 1.3M (OWID https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/population.csv?v=1&csvType=full&useColumnShortNames=true); the empire held Cambodia, much of Thailand and southern Laos, and occupied Champa (1190-1220).

urbanization.note: Educated guess. Greater Angkor 700,000-1,000,000 (Klassen et al.; Seshat 750,000-1,000,000) against an empire of 1.5-4M, but at low density sprawled over 1,000+ km2 (Angkor page).

activePersonnel.note: Educated guess. Standing force only: royal guard, palace and provincial retainers, royal elephants and war galleys; corvee levies are in trainedReserves. No count survives. Zhou Daguan (1296) describes soldiers fighting barefoot with lance and shield; an oral tradition told to Mouhot of 5-6 million soldiers is legend (Khmer Empire page). The Bayon reliefs show large armies on the Champa campaigns.

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess. Corvee levies called up by provincial lords: the spear-and-shield mass of the Bayon reliefs; Zhou Daguan says commoners were ordered to fight without preparation.

supportPersonnel.note: Educated guess. Mahouts (2 per elephant) and galley rowers (~30 per boat) of the royal establishment; carts and camp followers come with the levies.

mobilizationRatio.note: Educated guess. Corvee-based society where temple inscriptions list tens of thousands of assigned people (Ta Prohm 80,000); Zhou Daguan says commoners were ordered to fight in emergencies.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Educated guess. Royal guard and retainer spear-and-shield infantry; the levied mass of the Bayon reliefs is in trainedReserves.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: no armour according to Zhou Daguan

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: royal guard and lords' retainers

count.note: Educated guess. Standing archers and crossbowmen (bows shown on the Bayon reliefs).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5 minus. Evidence: simple bows; double-bow crossbows on elephants

count.note: Educated guess. Cham and Thai mercenaries in royal pay.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: professional mercenaries

count.note: Educated guess. Small horse contingent; Southeast Asian horses were few.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: small horses

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: nobles and retainers

count.note: Educated guess. War elephants carried nobles and mounted double-bow crossbows, possibly Cham mercenaries in Jayavarman VII's army (Jacq-Hergoualc'h via the Khmer Empire page). Arab writers credited Khmer kings with tens of thousands of elephants (claim).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: elephants with mounted crossbows

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: royal elephant stables

count.note: Educated guess. Oared war galleys on the Tonle Sap and Mekong; the Bayon and Banteay Chhmar show a naval battle against the Cham (Jayavarman VII page).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: river galleys

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: experienced against Champa

commandQuality.note: Rubric row: commandQuality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: Jayavarman VII expelled the Cham (1177-81) and conquered Champa (1190-91)

cohesion.note: Rubric row: cohesion 0.25-0.5. Evidence: levies under provincial lords, mercenaries

morale.note: Rubric row: morale 0.5-0.75. Evidence: recent victories, royal Buddhist kingship

weapons.note: Anchor: 3. Evidence: iron spears, bows, elephant-mounted double crossbows

armor.note: Anchor: between 1 and 2. Evidence: soldiers fought without armour (Zhou Daguan); shields only

ships.note: Anchor: between 2 (oared war galleys) and 3. Evidence: river war galleys

fortification.note: Anchor: 3 (ashlar walls). Evidence: Angkor Thom laterite walls 6-7 m high with moat and five gates (Khmer Empire page)

logistics.note: Anchor: 3 (engineered roads, depots). Evidence: raised highways with 121 rest houses and barays for water

communications.note: Anchor: 3. Evidence: royal roads and rest-house network

isr.note: Anchor: between 2 and 3. Evidence: no evidence of a formal intelligence system

gdpPerCapita.note: Educated guess. No Maddison series for mainland Southeast Asia before 1500. Placed below China 1150 (1,181) and near Egypt 1150 (1,052) (https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/gdp-per-capita-maddison-project-database.csv?v=1&csvType=full&useColumnShortNames=true).

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: Educated guess. Temple building absorbed much of the surplus; wars against Champa ongoing.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess. Stone construction, iron smelting at Preah Khan of Kompong Svay, crafts.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess. Rice with hydraulic works (barays) feeding a large urban complex.

annualCohort.note: population x 0.0095: Hansen 2006 (https://ancientportsantiques.com/wp-content/uploads/Documents/PLACES/GreeceContinental/Athens-Hansen2006.pdf, p. 34) puts a year class of 18-19-year-olds at ca. 1.9% of all males in a pre-modern age structure, i.e. ~0.95% of total population reaching military age per year (males only). Same model as the classical snapshots.

roadKm.note: Jayavarman VII built 121 rest houses roughly every 15 km along raised highways (Jayavarman VII page): 121 x 15 km = ~1,800 km.

majorPorts.note: Educated guess. River ports; Cham coastal ports under occupation.

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess. Chinese merchants carried most foreign trade.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. River transport and ox carts; monsoon limits the campaigning season.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Oxen, buffalo and elephants.

homeDefense.note: 1.2 row: walled capital and monsoon flooding the invader must cross; the Cham sack of 1177 shows the limits.

notes: Snapshot 1200 under Jayavarman VII, with Champa under Khmer occupation (1190-1220). No army count survives from any source; every force number is an educated guess, the weakest block in the file. Zhou Daguan (1296) is a century later. Population convention: Khmer-ruled lands including the Khorat plateau and central Thailand; occupied Champa partly counted in the high. Elephants and galleys are platforms; mahouts and rowers are supportPersonnel. Personnel: active = royal guard, retainers, mercenaries, royal elephants and galleys; trainedReserves = corvee levies; mobilizable = population x ratio.
